To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
GDR issuance increases the liquidity of underlying shares and that the increase is greater for shares that have less liquidity prior to GDR issuance.

GDR issuance by Indian firms can be explained by the presence of both global and local information asymmetry, illiquidity, and the SEC's Rule144A/RegS, and that these issuances are associated with significant home market stock price increases.

GDRs can help resolve global and local information asymmetry problems and that they do so even in the absence of liquidity enhancements and without the need to meet the disclosure requirements of US firms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of GDRs as a means for resolving information asymmetries and increasing liquidity.
the role that GDRs play in the international financial system.
the information content of GDRs and the role of the US market in facilitating the dissemination of information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GDRs were a good idea for the issuers, but not for the investors.
the GDRs are an important source of capital for Indian firms, and that they are also an important source of information to Indian investors.
GDR issuance is a means by which Indian firms resolve information asymmetries and improve liquidity, but that it is not the only means.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GDR issuance by Indian firms can be a useful way to resolve information asymmetries between firms and investors.
GDRs are a useful tool in reducing the costs of capital for Indian issuers, and that the benefits of GDR issuance outweigh the costs.
GDRs provide an efficient means of resolving information asymmetries and illiquidity in the home market.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SEC's Rule144A/Reg S regime can be a useful tool for resolving information asymmetries that impede the flow of capital across borders.
the information value of GDRs may be greater than the liquidity value.
GDRs are an effective mechanism to resolve information asymmetries that are not directly related to liquidity.
